    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:

turns.answer_text:
Rigid FTO/ITO, electron-selective SnO2 or fullerene-on-TiO2, a well-aligned HTL (Spiro/PTAA/PCDTBT), and Au or MoO3/Au minimize interface recombination and give the best MAPbI3 n-i-p cells in train.

**c064** clones the champion ETL (`TiO2-c | SnO2-np`: compact hole-block + SnO2 CB ~−4.4 eV, high μe) with Spiro/Au — the reference selective hole contact. **c005** is essentially the 19.35% device: PCBM passivates TiO2/perovskite traps; PCDTBT’s deep HOMO raises Voc; MoO3|Au is ohmic. **c013** adds a thin ferroelectric P(VDF-TrFE) tunnel/passivation layer on the HTL side (same class as PMMA|Spiro 18.0% and IEICO-4F|Spiro 19.0%) plus MoO3|Ag. **c017** is the vacuum n-i-p analog of 17.9%: PhIm-doped C60 and F6-TCNNQ-doped TaTm are highly conductive and selective; co-evaporated MAPbI3 is compact (Ag vs Au is a small penalty). **c031** is the 16.54% `SnO2-c | TiO2-c`/Spiro/Au stack plus mp-SnO2 for collection.

Final: c064, c005, c013, c017, c031
